qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Exclusive state-granted utility franchises (CPUC, PUCT) operating critical electric and gas transmission/distribution networks (SDG&E, SoCalGas, Oncor) with unreplicable rights-of-way and captive rate-payers. Statutory cost-of-service ratemaking provides authorized ROE (~9.5-10.2%) with fuel and operating cost pass-through. Erosion risks center on California inverse condemnation wildfire liabilities, political scrutiny of utility bills, and long-term decarbonization pressure on gas distribution.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Balance Sheet & Cash Conversion). Regulated utility monopoly (SDG&E, SoCalGas, Oncor) with unreplicable physical T&D infrastructure, but suffers from structural utility capital drag: median ROIC of 4.5%, perpetual negative free cash flow after capex ($10.6B capex vs $4.6B OCF in FY2025), extreme debt leverage ($29.0B long-term debt vs $1.8B net income = 15.8x), and weak interest coverage of 2.2x requiring continuous capital market access.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC is 4.5% (2016-2025 range 3.2%-7.3%). Free cash flow after capex has been negative in 8 of the last 10 years, with FY2025 capex reaching $10.6B against OCF of $4.6B. Long-term debt expanded from $14.4B in 2016 to $29.0B in 2025 ($36.7B total debt) with cash of only $29M. TTM interest expense of $1,532M against EBIT of $3,321M leaves interest coverage thin at 2.17x. California inverse condemnation risk and S&P BBB+ rating with negative outlook reflect structural reliance on external debt and equity markets to fund the regulated asset base.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
